name_reason: Compliant with data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention: domain=graphics, descriptor encodes purpose (chapter ambient palette animation pacing) and data-type role (tick_latch = timer snapshot). No Ghidra address residue (no hex suffix equal to its own or another address). No domain ID to preserve. Name accurately reflects both purpose and the 4-byte timer-snapshot data type.
purpose: BIOS-tick snapshot that paces the slow chapter ambient-palette animation cycle: stores the BDA tick value at which the ambient-palette index (0x53C0B) last advanced.
logic_summary: Seeded once at startup in main (latch = (int32)(int16)*[0x46C]) before the animation tick ever reads it. Each frame, fd2_tick_chapter_palette_animation computes delta = (int32)(int16)*[0x46C] - latch; if delta > 4 (signed) or delta < 0 (wrap), it advances the ambient-palette index (0..3 wrap) and re-latches to the current tick. The fast walk-anim alt index (0x53C07) advances every call independently of this latch.
element_semantics: Single scalar: a BIOS/BDA timer-tick snapshot. Source value is MOVSX of the 16-bit BDA tick counter at word [0x46C] sign-extended to 32 bits. Read via signed elapsed-tick deltas (SUB then signed CMP JG / TEST JGE), so semantically a signed timer snapshot; storage and every access are full 32-bit dword, hence uint32 to match slot width.
notes: Data address (not a function): get_plate_comment returns 'No function at address' and get_xrefs_from returns none, so there is no stored Ghidra data plate to update; the listing context block is decompiler-generated. Memory is all-zero (BSS, zero-init). Writers: main @ 0x25D8B (startup seed), fd2_tick_chapter_palette_animation @ 0x129CD (re-latch). Readers: fd2_tick_chapter_palette_animation @ 0x1298F, 0x129A2. is_const=false because the game writes it. Disassembly at 0x1298F-0x129CD verified every claim in the src comment block (SUB EAX,[0x53C0F]; CMP 0x4/JG; TEST/JGE; MOV [0x53C0F],EAX). src/life/main.c comment already accurate, precise, ASCII-only, well-structured -> keep, no edit made. Confirmed via Grep that palette.c also references this global (read side) and globals.h declares it; neither touched per single-symbol scope.
